title: Florida Atlantic University Awarded $400,000 NSF Grant to Expand Post-Quantum Cryptographic Protocols - Quantum Computing Report
gist: The NSF awarded Florida Atlantic University a $399,964 three-year grant (Award No. 2528909, May 2026 to April 2029) led by Edoardo Persichetti and Veronika Kuchta to build post-quantum cryptographic protocols beyond NIST's basic primitives. The work targets blind, threshold and multisignatures and verifiable random functions for decentralized systems and distributed ledgers, using lattices, error-correcting codes, group actions and isogenies.

insights.claim: The NSF awarded a $399,964 grant (Award No. 2528909) to Florida Atlantic University's Charles E. Schmidt College of Science for a three-year project (May 15, 2026 to April 30, 2029) to develop cryptographic primitives that secure decentralized systems and digital infrastructure against future quantum attacks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Small but continuing federal funding for PQC research beyond NIST standards; signals US government focus on quantum-safe decentralized infrastructure.

insights.claim: The FAU PQC project is led by Dr. Edoardo Persichetti, director of FAU's Center for Cryptology and Information Security, with co-principal investigator Dr. Veronika Kuchta.
